title: Security integration ops: RBAC v2 -> audit flow -> SIEM export
summary: Operational guide tying RBAC v2 decisions to audit schema, automated evidence packaging, and SIEM export for private deployments (VPC + firewall + mTLS). Focused on compliance evidence automation and reliable downstream ingestion.
content:
Purpose
This document defines an operational integration between RBAC v2, audit logging schema, evidence automation pipelines, and SIEM export for Redwood Private deployments. Target audience: SREs, infra security engineers, compliance engineers, and solutions engineers prepping customer evidence bundles.

Scope
- Applies to Private control plane and customer-managed dataplane (VPC, peered subnets, on-prem variants).
- Covers how RBAC decisions are logged, how logs are shaped into an audit schema, packaging for evidence automation, and recommended SIEM export formats and retention/PII handling.
- Excludes application-level business logs that customers own.

High-level flow
1) AuthN/AuthZ: identity request (OIDC/PKI/SAML) => Redwood control plane enforces RBAC v2 policy.
2) Enforcement event: every allow/deny, policy-eval, escalation, and policy-change emits structured audit event.
3) Local collector: host-agent (filebeat/rsyslog) enriches with network context (VPC id, subnet, security-group id).
4) Evidence automation: daily/weekly job queries the audit store, packages signed artifacts, and pushes to encrypted evidence buckets.
5) SIEM export: streaming (Kafka/Logstash) or periodic bulk (S3 -> SIEM) to customer SIEM.

RBAC v2 model (operational notes)
- Roles: system-admin, infra-ops, customer-admin, service-account, readonly-audit.
- Principals: human (OIDC email), machine (mTLS identity / SPIFFE SVID), external (SAML group mapped).
- Policies: expressed as allow/deny rules with resource-scoped selectors. Policies are versioned; policy-change events must be audited with before/after diffs.
- Constraints: time-bound grants (expirable role bindings), emergency-break-glass events flagged and require 2nd-person approval.

Audit log schema (canonical JSON event) - fields and examples
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC string (e.g., 2026-03-10T14:22:31Z)
- event_id: UUIDv4
- service: string (e.g., "control-plane", "inference-gateway")
- event_type: string (authz_decision | authn | policy_change | system_alert | network_acl_change)
- outcome: string (allow | deny | error | unknown)
- principal: { "id": "svc:encoder-42", "type": "service_account", "issuer": "spiffe://redwood.local" }  -- (flattened into principal_id, principal_type, principal_issuer for storage systems that avoid nested objects)
- resource: string (resource path or id, e.g., "model/llama-2/rate_limit/key-123")
- action: string (e.g., generate, fetch-kv-cache, update-policy)
- request_context: string (short summary of request attributes)
- network_context: string (vpc_id=subnet=src_ip=src_port)
- decision_trace: string (policy ids evaluated; deterministic ordered list)
- request_id: correlation id for tracing
- raw_payload: base64(JSON) of original request (when allowed)
- signature: detached signature (kms-key-id + base64 sig)
- retention_class: string (audit | evidence | ephemeral)

Operational notes on schema:
- Keep events flat for easy indexing in Elasticsearch/Cloud SIEM. Provide both flattened and nested variants where supported.
- For PII-sensitive payloads, raw_payload must be redacted at source and only kept in evidence-class artifacts with restricted access and short-lived signed URLs.

Collector and enrichment pipeline
- Local collector (recommended): filebeat -> central Kafka -> log-enricher (adds VPC metadata, instance tags, security group IDs, subnet CIDR name) -> audit-store (write-once S3 + indexer).
- Agent config snippets: set filebeat fields: service:control-plane, cluster:customer-<id>, vpc_id: <env.VPC_ID>. Ensure TLS with client certs to Kafka.

SIEM export patterns
- Streaming: produce to topic "audit.events" in JSON lines. Use Avro/Schema registry for strict schema evolution.
- Bulk: daily partitioned S3 drop, path convention: s3://<customer-evidence>/<year>=YYYY/<month>=MM/<day>=DD/audit-events-<shard>.json.gz. Provide manifest.json with SHA256 checksums and GPG signature.
- Formats supported: newline-delimited JSON (preferred), ECS-compliant mapping for Elastic SIEM, CEF mapping examples for legacy SIEMs.

Example SIEM mapping (ECS style)
- event.id -> event_id
- event.action -> action
- event.outcome -> outcome
- user.id -> principal_id
- network.transport + source.ip -> network_context (split during ingestion)
- process.name -> service

Evidence automation (packaging and proof)
- Objectives: produce tamper-evident archive for audit review with: log slices, policy diffs, signed manifests, key/certificate snapshots, and an evidence README.
- Pipeline steps:
  a) Query audit-store for date-range and filters (policy_change, authz_decision).
  b) Collect policy versions from policy-store (git tag or policy DB snapshot).
  c) Attach PKI state: CA certs, CRL at time-bound, and service certificate fingerprints. Do NOT include private keys.
  d) Generate manifest.json with checksums and a provenance file (who exported it, JIRA ticket linking the request).
  e) Sign manifest with KMS asymmetric key and include signature.asc.
  f) Upload to encrypted S3 bucket with object lock enabled (WORM), set lifecycle to meet retention policy.
- Access: evidence buckets are ACLed to a narrow role; requestors use short-lived presigned URLs.

Network architecture patterns for Private deployments (VPC + transit)
- Pattern A: Single-tenant VPC per customer. Subnets: control-plane (private), compute (gpu-pool), infra (bastion + NAT), logging (S3 egress gateway).
- Pattern B: Shared transit VPC with per-customer isolated subnets using security-group + namespace isolation. Useful for many small customers to save infra.
- Pattern C: On-prem air-gapped—local relay appliance (signed ingestion gateway) that pushes encrypted bundles to a physical handoff or to a customer-managed queue.

Firewall rules / ACL recommendations (examples)
- Control plane inbound: allow 0.0.0.0/0 TCP 443 only to API gateway with WAF. Behind WAF further restrict by client cert and JWT validation.
- Dataplane (GPU) egress: restrict to customer-controlled destinations and allow only to telemetry endpoints (kafka/logging endpoint) on known ports.
- Internal: service-to-service only via mTLS; block all plain-text ports.
- Example SG rule (AWS security group style):
  - sg-control-plane: inbound TCP 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 (WAF), inbound TCP 22 from admin-cidr, outbound TCP 443 to logging-endpoints
  - sg-gpu-pool: inbound TCP 10250 from sg-control-plane, inbound TCP 9400 from monitoring-nodes, outbound TCP 443 to s3 (policy: https only)

mTLS for service-to-service (recommended backbone)
- Identity: SPIFFE IDs issued by a local SPIRE deployment or by vault PKI for short-lived certs.
- Trust model: Root CA in HSM/KMS, intermediate in SPIRE, nodes obtain SVIDs with TTL <= 1h.
- Rotation: automatic rotation via SPIRE with 2-minute grace; certs rotated without downtime using connection draining.
- Verification: enforce SAN check and expected SPIFFE path; reject certs without expected audience.
- Fallback: allow JWT bearer with audience claim in cross-zone edge cases but log as degraded enforcement and emit metric meter.authz.degraded.

Hardening checklist (practical runbook)
1) RBAC
   - Ensure every policy change requires a signed change entry and ticket id.
   - Enforce least privilege default role and use time-limited bindings for sensitive roles.
2) Logging
   - Enable structured JSON audit logs on all control-plane components.
   - Ensure request_id is propagated from ingress -> backend -> logs.
3) Log integrity
   - Sign daily log bundles with KMS and store checksums in manifest.
   - Enable object lock for evidence buckets.
4) Network
   - Block unnecessary egress with explicit allow lists.
   - Use private endpoints for cloud APIs (no public egress where possible).
5) mTLS/Pki
   - Deploy SPIRE or equivalent; enforce SVID checks.
   - Automate cert rotation and verify via canary test.
6) SIEM export
   - Use schema-registry for topic schemas.
   - Validate sample exports end-to-end and maintain replayable manifests.
7) Access control
   - Restrict evidence exports to a minimal role with MFA and approval workflow.
8) Evidence handling
   - Redact PII from routine exports; keep full payloads only in sealed evidence bundles.
9) Testing
   - Weekly smoke: simulate policy_rollout + deny event and verify that audit event appears and is exported.
   - Quarterly: full evidence build rehearsal for a sample timeframe.
10) Incident response
   - If audit-store is tampered, freeze exports, snapshot state, and notify compliance+legal.

Operational run examples (short playbooks)
- Playbook: Respond to a requested evidence export for a customer compliance audit
  1) Create JIRA request RDINF-EVID-<id> with scope and retention date.
  2) Approve via 2-person review.
  3) Run evidence-collector --start <date> --end <date> --policies=all --sign-with=kms://projects/keys/exporter-key
  4) Upload artifacts to presigned customer bucket and add ticket comment with link.

- Playbook: SIEM ingestion failure handling
  1) Detect via exporter.sink.failures > 0 alert.
  2) Fallback to bulk S3 drop and set export_mode=bulk in manifest.
  3) Create a non-blocking alert to security-oncall and re-play the missing partitions.

Diagrams
- Logical flow (ASCII):
  [Identity Provider] -> [Control Plane (RBAC v2)] -> [Audit Emitter] -> [Local Collector/Enricher] -> [Kafka/Topic audit.events] -> [Log-indexer / SIEM adapter] -> [SIEM]

- Network sketch (ASCII):
  Internet -> WAF -> API-GW (Client cert check) -+-> Control plane (private subnet)
                                               |
                                               +-> Transit VPC -> GPU pools (private subnets, mTLS)

Notes and open questions
- Consider adding a checksum ledger (blockchain-style append-only log) for higher-assurance tamper evidence.
- Evaluate whether SPIRE is mandatory or if short-lived Vault certs suffice for smaller customers.
- Determine maximum tolerated retention for raw_payload under GDPR contracts.

Appendices
A) Example minimal flattened audit event (newline-delimited JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-03-10T14:22:31Z",
  "event_id": "c1b2f9a6-3d6a-4c01-9d2e-1234567890ab",
  "service": "control-plane",
  "event_type": "authz_decision",
  "outcome": "deny",
  "principal_id": "user:alice@redwood.com",
  "principal_type": "human",
  "resource": "model/llama-2:invoke",
  "action": "generate",
  "network_context": "vpc-0a1b2c=subnet-1234=10.10.4.21=51234",
  "decision_trace": "pol-234,pol-231",
  "request_id": "req-20260310-abcdef",
  "retention_class": "audit"
}

B) Quick checklist for oncall to validate export
- Verify manifest presence and signature.asc valid with exporter KMS key.
- Check SHA256 of first and last shard in manifest matches objects.
- Confirm S3 lifecycle is set (object lock + encryption).
